executionHistory.summary: Completed SCOPE-028-04 (Integration, Snapshot, Compatibility, Performance, and Release Proof), the final scope. Found and fixed a real production gap in volatility-sizing-lab.html (rlvol.js untouched): roughnessBuildInput() hard-coded source.freshness to 'fresh' whenever cached rows existed, discarding RLDATA.barInfo()'s own real fresh/stale/missing computation, so a genuinely stale-but-usable cache was silently mislabeled fresh to the diagnostic. Fixed additively: readCachedBars() now carries info.state through as cacheFreshness on the bars snapshot; enableRoughness()'s no-cache fallback declares cacheFreshness:'missing'; roughnessBuildInput() passes the real snapshot freshness through as source.freshness instead of a hard-coded literal; renderRoughnessEvidence() now renders an explicit 'Source is STALE as of <retrievedAt>...' sentence when the diagnostic's source is stale. Six new persistent tests were added and executed, all passing: TP-028-04-01 (tests/volatility-roughness.integration.mjs, 'Regression: SCN-028-011 evaluates one immutable cached snapshot without ensureBars') proves the real formula computes from a stale-labeled input without withholding merely for staleness, carries source timing through unmodified, and that rlvol.js's own source text calls no ensureBars/hydrate/fetch; TP-028-04-02 (same file, 'SCN-028-012 browser-global and CommonJS diagnostics are canonically identical') loads rlvol.js a second time under node:vm with no module object to force the UMD browser-global branch, running the identical start/step/finalize composition across batch sizes 1/7/25/remainder in both realms and asserting byte-identical RLVOL.canonicalize() output and diagnosticId;
